gancho: Acusado de vender um tesouro nacional, um Vermeer, ao nazista Göring, o holandês Han van Meegeren se defendeu dizendo que o quadro era falso, feito por ele. Para provar, pintou outro "Vermeer" diante de testemunhas.
explicacao: Van Meegeren queria ser reconhecido como pintor, mas a crítica desprezava seu trabalho. Resolveu então provar seu talento imitando os mestres holandeses do século XVII, e grandes especialistas da época aceitaram seus quadros como autênticos. Em 1937, o historiador Abraham Bredius saudou a sua "Ceia em Emaús" como "a obra-prima" de Vermeer. Durante a ocupação alemã, Hermann Göring trocou 137 pinturas saqueadas por outro falso Vermeer, "Cristo e a Adúltera". Em maio de 1945, os Aliados acharam o quadro numa mina de sal na Áustria e chegaram até o pintor. Preso como colaborador, ele corria o risco de pena de morte. Confessou a fraude e, entre julho e dezembro de 1945, pintou um último quadro no estilo de Vermeer, "Jesus entre os Doutores", acompanhado por repórteres e testemunhas nomeadas pela Justiça. A prova química veio depois: as tintas tinham baquelite, uma resina do século XX. Ele a misturava à tinta e assava a tela no forno para endurecê-la e simular 300 anos de secagem. Como o quadro de Göring era falso, não era patrimônio holandês, e a acusação de colaboração caiu. Em novembro de 1947, ele foi condenado a um ano de prisão por falsificação e fraude, mas morreu menos de dois meses depois, após dois ataques cardíacos, ainda à espera de ser levado à cadeia.

fontes.trecho: Van Meegeren became a national hero after World War II when it was revealed that he had sold a forged painting to Reichsmarschall Hermann Göring during the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands. Van Meegeren attempted to make a career as an artist, but art critics dismissed his work. He decided to prove his talent by forging paintings from the Dutch Golden Age. Leading experts of the time accepted his paintings as genuine 17th-century works [...] Facing a possible death penalty, he confessed that the painting was a forgery, and was subsequently convicted and sentenced to one year in prison. However, he died less than two months later after suffering two heart attacks. [...] In September 1937, Bredius examined The Supper at Emmaus and, writing in The Burlington Magazine, he accepted it as a genuine Vermeer and praised it very highly as "the masterpiece of Johannes Vermeer of Delft". [...] He came up with a way to use phenol formaldehyde (Bakelite) to make paints harden after application, making paintings appear 300 years old (through the illusion that the paint had already dried for that long). [...] after completing a painting, he would bake it at 100 °C (212 °F) to 120 °C (248 °F) to harden the paint [...] Nazi Reichsmarschall Hermann Göring traded 137 looted paintings for Christ with the Adulteress. On 25 August 1943, Göring hid his collection of looted artwork, including Christ with the Adulteress, in an Austrian salt mine [...] On 17 May 1945, Allied forces entered the salt mine and Captain Harry Anderson discovered the painting. [...] Based on Miedl's confession, the painting was traced back to Van Meegeren. On 29 May 1945, he was arrested and charged with fraud and aiding and abetting the enemy. [...] Van Meegeren painted his last forgery between July and December 1945 watched by reporters and court-appointed witnesses: Jesus among the Doctors, also called Young Christ in the Temple, not a copy but in the style of Vermeer. [...] He found that the paint contained the phenolformaldehyde resins Bakelite and Albertol, not invented until the 20th century, as paint hardeners [...] The collaboration charges had been dropped, since the expert panel had found that the supposed Vermeer sold to Hermann Göring had been a forgery and was, therefore, not the cultural property of the Netherlands. [...] On 12 November 1947, the Fourth Chamber of the Amsterdam Regional Court found Han van Meegeren guilty of forgery and fraud, and sentenced him to one year in prison. [...] While waiting to be moved to prison, Van Meegeren returned to his home

gancho: Em 1990, dois homens vestidos de policiais levaram 13 obras de um museu de Boston, entre elas um Vermeer. O caso nunca foi resolvido, e as molduras vazias continuam penduradas nas paredes, à espera das obras.
explicacao: Na madrugada de 18 de março de 1990, os guardas do Museu Isabella Stewart Gardner deixaram entrar dois homens disfarçados de policiais, que diziam atender a um chamado. Os ladrões amarraram os guardas e passaram cerca de uma hora no prédio. Levaram 13 peças, entre elas "O Concerto", um dos apenas 34 quadros conhecidos de Vermeer, e "A Tempestade no Mar da Galileia", a única marinha de Rembrandt. A escolha intriga os especialistas: obras valiosas de Rafael, Botticelli e Michelangelo ficaram intactas, enquanto um ornamento de águia quase sem valor foi levado. Outro enigma: os sensores de movimento não registraram ninguém na sala de onde saiu um quadro de Manet, a não ser um dos próprios guardas em suas rondas. O museu não tinha seguro, e o testamento de Isabella Gardner determinou que nada da coleção fosse mudado de lugar. Por isso as molduras vazias seguem nas paredes, como homenagem e à espera da volta das obras. Ninguém foi preso e nada foi recuperado. O FBI acredita que o roubo foi planejado por uma quadrilha, e o museu oferece uma recompensa de 10 milhões de dólares, a maior já oferecida por uma instituição privada.

fontes.trecho: In the early hours of March 18, 1990, 13 works of art were stolen from the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum in Boston. Security guards admitted two men posing as policemen responding to a disturbance call, and the thieves bound the guards and looted the museum over the next hour. The case is unsolved; no arrests have been made, and no works have been recovered. [...] The museum offers a $10 million reward for information leading to the art's recovery, the largest bounty ever offered by a private institution. [...] Among them was The Concert, one of only 34 known paintings by Johannes Vermeer and thought to be the most valuable unrecovered painting in the world. Also missing is The Storm on the Sea of Galilee, Rembrandt's only seascape. [...] The FBI believes that the robbery was planned by a criminal gang. [...] it lacked a climate control system and an insurance policy [...] The museum's motion detectors did not detect any motion within the Blue Room during the thieves' time in the building. The only footsteps detected in the room that night were Abath's during the two times when he p [...] Chez Tortoni by French painter Édouard Manet (1832–1883) was taken from the Blue Room [...] the thieves passed other valuable works by Raphael, Botticelli and Michelangelo and left them undisturbed, opting to take relatively valueless items such as the gu and finial. [...] As Gardner's will decreed that nothing in her collection should be moved, the empty frames for the stolen paintings remain hanging in their respective locations in the museum as placeholders for their potential return. [...] empty frames remain hanging both in homage to the missing works and as placeholders for their return.

gancho: Em 1983, a revista Stern pagou 9,3 milhões de marcos por sessenta volumes de diários de Hitler. Eram falsos, e peritos aprovaram a letra comparando-a com "amostras" que, sem eles saberem, vinham do mesmo falsário.
explicacao: O autor era Konrad Kujau, que já vendia objetos nazistas e forjou os volumes entre 1981 e 1983. Ele imitava bem a caligrafia de Hitler, mas o resto era tosco. Usou cadernos baratos comprados em Berlim Oriental, tinta diluída em água para correr numa caneta moderna e chá espalhado nas páginas para envelhecê-las. Na capa, quis pôr as iniciais "AH" com letras de plástico de uma loja de departamentos e, por engano, colou "FH". Para autenticar os diários, a revista enviou aos peritos uma única página e, para comparação, documentos supostamente escritos por Hitler que também eram falsificações de Kujau. Os peritos concluíram que a letra era genuína. O historiador Hugh Trevor-Roper, especialista na Alemanha nazista, também declarou os diários autênticos, mas mudou de ideia na entrevista coletiva do lançamento. A farsa caiu quando o Arquivo Federal alemão fez a análise forense que faltava: sob luz ultravioleta, o papel tinha um componente fluorescente que não deveria existir num documento antigo, e a encadernação de um volume tinha poliéster, que não era fabricado antes de 1953. Kujau e Gerd Heidemann, que participou da compra pela revista e desviou parte do dinheiro, foram presos.

fontes.trecho: The Hitler Diaries (Hitler-Tagebücher) were a series of sixty volumes of journals purportedly written by Adolf Hitler, but forged by Konrad Kujau between 1981 and 1983. The diaries were purchased in 1983 for 9.3 million Deutsche Marks (£2.3 million or $3.7 million) by the West German news magazine Stern [...] the historian Hugh Trevor-Roper, to authenticate the diaries; he did so, pronouncing them genuine. At the press conference to announce the publication, Trevor-Roper announced that on reflection he had changed his mind [...] Rigorous forensic analysis, which had not been performed previously, quickly confirmed that the diaries were fakes. [...] In the mid-1970s he began selling Nazi memorabilia [...] " the diaries and was involved in their purchase was Gerd Heidemann, who had an obsession with the Nazis. When Stern started buying the diaries, Heidemann stole a significant proportion of the money. Kujau and Heidemann spent time in prison for their parts in the fraud [...] was a specialist on Nazi Germany [...] He forged passable imitations of his subjects' genuine handwriting, but the rest of the work was crude [...] Kujau used one of a pile of notebooks he had bought cheaply in East Berlin, and attempted to put the letters "AH" in gold on the front—purchasing plastic, Hong Kong-made letters from a department store, he inadvertently used "FH" rather than "AH". [...] mixed them with water so it would flow more easily from the cheap modern pen he used. Finally he sprinkled tea over the pages [...] They also did not give the forensic specialists an entire diary, but removed one page only. For comparison purposes they also provided the experts with other samples of Hitler's writing, a handwritten draft for a telegram: this was from Heidemann's own collection and had also been forged by Kujau. Within days Walde provided further documents for comparison—all Kujau forgeries. [...] From the samples provided, the experts concluded that the handwriting was genuine. [...] passed three complete diaries to Henke at the Bundesarchiv for a more complete forensic examination. [...] ultraviolet light had shown a fluorescent element to the paper, which should not have been present in an old document, and that the bindings of one of the diaries included polyester which had not been made before 1953.

gancho: O falsário Wolfgang Beltracchi passou anos vendendo "obras perdidas" de pintores modernos. Caiu quando, uma única vez, usou tinta pronta: o tubo tinha branco de titânio, pigmento ainda não vendido em 1914.
explicacao: Beltracchi não copiava quadros conhecidos. Pintava obras novas no estilo de artistas como Max Ernst, Fernand Léger e Heinrich Campendonk, às vezes dizendo que eram obras perdidas, conhecidas só pelo título em documentos e catálogos antigos. Com a mulher, Helene, inventou uma origem para os quadros: teriam sido do avô dela, o industrial Werner Jägers, que os teria comprado do marchand judeu Alfred Flechtheim. Quando a história foi questionada, ele forjou provas: com câmera e filme antigos, fotografou uma mulher numa sala com os quadros ao fundo. Era Helene, vestida como a própria avó. Etiquetas falsas da coleção Flechtheim completavam o pacote. A falha veio com "Quadro vermelho com cavalos", atribuído a Campendonk e vendido por 2,88 milhões de euros. Uma análise de 2008 achou na tinta branco de titânio, que ainda não estava disponível em 1914 e nem constava no rótulo do tubo holandês que ele usou. Segundo o próprio Beltracchi, foi a única vez em que ele não misturou a própria tinta. A versão do avô também tinha furos: Jägers era adolescente nos anos 1930 e foi membro do Partido Nazista. Em 2011, Beltracchi foi condenado a seis anos de prisão por falsificar 14 obras, vendidas por um total de 45 milhões de dólares. Ele diz ter imitado cerca de 50 artistas.

fontes.trecho: Beltracchi, together with his wife Helene, sold forgeries of alleged works by famous artists, including Max Ernst, Heinrich Campendonk, Fernand Léger, and Kees van Dongen. Though he was found guilty for forging 14 works of art that sold for a combined $45m (£28.6m), he claims to have faked "about 50" artists. [...] In 2011, after a 40-day trial, Beltracchi was found guilty and sentenced to six years in a German prison. [...] Beltracchi did not copy existing and well known paintings, but painted his own paintings imitating the style of the artists in question. He made up the titles and motives, or claimed that a painting of his was a lost work that was only known by its title in old documents or catalogs. He and his wife also established a false provenance for the works, claiming that Helene Beltracchi's grandfather—the wealthy industrialist Werner Jägers—had been friends with the German-Jewish art dealer Alfred Flechtheim in the 1920s. They claimed that Flechtheim sold a cache of works to Jägers [...] Secondly, Jägers was a teenager in the 1930s [...] Jägers had been a member of the Nazi Party in the 1930s [...] When the credibility of the story was questioned, the Beltracchis constructed "proof" that the paintings had been in the family since the 1920s. They delivered photographs seemingly of Helene Beltracchi's grandmother in a room with the paintings in question in the background. In reality, the photographs had been produced by Wolfgang Beltracchi himself using an antique camera and film; the woman on the photographs being Helene Beltracchi, dressed up as her own grandmother. They also created fake labels proclaiming that the paintings were from the "Sammlung Flechtheim" [...] The painting was then sold to a company in Malta for €2.88 million. Beltracchi had used a paint tube produced in the Netherlands. Technical analysis by Nicholas Eastaugh revealed that the paint contained titanium white (which was not specified on the label), a pigment that had not been in use in Campendonk's times. As Beltracchi remembered, because he had not mixed his own paint this one time, the forgery was uncovered. [...] "Rotes Bild mit Pferden" was found to be fake by Artvera's gallery, based in Switzerland. In 2008, a scientific analysis showed the painting contained titanium white, which was not yet available in 1914.

gancho: No dia da abertura da Olimpíada de Inverno de 1994, ladrões levaram "O Grito", de Munch, da Galeria Nacional de Oslo e deixaram um bilhete: "Obrigado pela segurança ruim".
explicacao: A Noruega sediava os Jogos de Lillehammer, e o quadro tinha sido levado para uma galeria do segundo andar como parte das festividades olímpicas. Em 12 de fevereiro de 1994, data da cerimônia de abertura, dois homens invadiram o museu e saíram com ele. Em março, a galeria se recusou a pagar um resgate de 1 milhão de dólares. A polícia norueguesa armou então uma operação disfarçada, com ajuda da polícia britânica e do Museu Getty, e a pintura foi recuperada sem danos em 7 de maio. Em 1996, quatro homens foram condenados, entre eles Pål Enger, que já tinha sido condenado em 1988 por roubar outro quadro de Munch, "Amor e Dor". A história, porém, teve uma reviravolta: eles acabaram soltos em recurso, por questões legais, porque os agentes britânicos da operação tinham entrado na Noruega com identidades falsas. O quadro tem mais de uma versão, e a de 1910 foi roubada em 2004, à luz do dia, por homens armados e mascarados que entraram no Museu Munch, em Oslo. Em 2018, a dupla de humoristas noruegueses Ylvis fez um musical sobre o roubo de 1994, estrelado pelo próprio Enger.

fontes.trecho: On 12 February 1994, the same day as the opening of the 1994 Winter Olympics in Lillehammer, two men broke into the National Gallery, Oslo, and stole its version of The Scream, leaving a note reading "Thanks for the poor security". The painting had been moved down to a second-story gallery as part of the Olympic festivities. After the gallery refused to pay a ransom demand of US$1 million in March 1994, Norwegian police set up a sting operation with assistance from the British police (SO10) and the Getty Museum and the painting was recovered undamaged on 7 May 1994. In January 1996, four men were convicted in connection with the theft, including Pål Enger, who had been convicted of stealing Munch's Love and Pain in 1988. They were released on appeal on legal grounds: the British agents involved in the sting operation had entered Norway under false identities. [...] The 1910 version of The Scream was stolen on 22 August 2004, during daylight hours, when masked gunmen entered the Munch Museum in Oslo [...] In 2018 Norwegian comedy duo Ylvis made a musical based on the painting's theft starring Pål Enger who stole it in 1994.

gancho: O falsário inglês Tom Keating escondia armadilhas nos próprios quadros: escrevia mensagens em branco de chumbo sob a pintura, visíveis num raio X, ou punha glicerina embaixo, para a tinta se desfazer numa limpeza.
explicacao: Keating, que viveu de 1917 a 1984, era restaurador e dizia ter falsificado mais de 2 mil quadros de mais de 160 artistas. Ele se dizia socialista e movia uma espécie de vingança contra marchands que, para ele, exploravam artistas e compradores. Por isso deixava pistas de propósito, para que restauradores e conservadores descobrissem o engano. A glicerina funcionava assim: na limpeza, os solventes a dissolviam, e a camada de tinta por cima se desmanchava, denunciando a falsificação. Ele também usava acrílicos e vernizes modernos em quadros supostamente de séculos passados. Nos anos 1950, depois que ele espalhou falsificações do pintor Cornelius Krieghoff, surgiram tantos Krieghoff "recém-descobertos" que os preços despencaram, pelo medo de que muitos fossem falsos. Quem chegou até ele foi a jornalista Geraldine Norman, do Times de Londres. Em 1976, ela publicou que treze quadros inéditos de Samuel Palmer, surgidos no mercado em dez anos, eram falsos, e que cinco tinham vindo de uma mesma fonte, a parceira de Keating, Jane Kelly. Os dois foram a julgamento em 1979, mas ele desmaiou no banco das testemunhas e, por causa da saúde frágil, acabou liberado sem acusação. Em 1982, estrelou uma série premiada de TV, no Channel 4, ensinando as técnicas dos velhos mestres.

fontes.trecho: Thomas Patrick Keating (1 March 1917 – 12 February 1984) was an English artist, art restorer and art forger. Considered the most prolific and versatile art forger of the 20th century, he claimed to have faked more than 2000 paintings by more than 160 different artists [...] Keating's main objective was a vendetta against corrupt, predatory art dealers whom he believed victimised both artists and the buying public. [...] At one point in the 1950s, so many "newly-discovered" Krieghoffs had come on the market that prices were acutely depressed, over fears many were fake [...] Keating considered himself a socialist and used his political views to rationalize his actions. He deliberately left clues to equip fellow art restorers, conservators and merchants to discover his deception. Sometimes he would put a layer of glycerine under oil paint so that when a picture would be cleaned the solvents would dissolve the glycerin and the paint layer would disintegrate, revealing the picture as a fake. Or when beginning a picture, he would paint messages on canvases in lead white that could easily be revealed with x-rays. [...] He would also use modern acrylics and varnishes on paintings supposedly from previous centuries. [...] both Keating and Kelly ended up on trial, in 1979 [...] In February 1970, Geraldine Norman, sale room correspondent for The Times of London [...] In July 1976 the first of a series of articles by Norman on fake Palmers was published on page one of The Times. Thirteen previously unknown Palmers that had appeared on the market in the past decade were all declared fake. Five of them had come from a single source: Jane Ke [...] he collapsed in the witness box, and was taken back to hospital. He was released without charge two weeks later due to failing health. In 1982, he starred in an award-winning Channel 4 television series in which he instructed viewers in the intricately detailed painting techniques of his favourite Old Masters.

gancho: Em 1934, roubaram um painel do Retábulo de Gante, obra-prima dos Van Eyck. O suposto ladrão disse no leito de morte que só ele sabia onde a peça estava e que levaria o segredo para o túmulo. Ela nunca foi achada.
explicacao: O painel "Os Juízes Justos", pintado entre 1430 e 1432, ficava com o resto do retábulo na Catedral de São Bavão, em Gante, na Bélgica, até sumir na noite de 10 de abril de 1934. Semanas depois, o bispo recebeu um pedido de resgate de um milhão de francos belgas, que o governo recusou. Seguiu-se uma troca de pelo menos 11 cartas, e, como gesto de boa-fé, quem pedia o resgate devolveu uma das duas partes do painel, uma figura de São João Batista pintada em tons de cinza. Em 25 de novembro, Arsène Goedertier revelou ao advogado, no leito de morte, que só ele sabia onde a obra estava. Entre seus papéis havia cópias das cartas de resgate e um bilhete nunca enviado, dizendo que o painel repousava num lugar de onde ninguém o tiraria sem chamar a atenção do público. A polícia concluiu que ele era o ladrão. Houve buscas extensas, entre elas um raio X da catedral inteira até 10 metros de profundidade, e hoje se acredita que o painel foi destruído. No lugar dele, desde 1945, fica uma cópia feita pelo restaurador Jef Van der Veken, que deixou uma pista sutil de que era cópia: deu a um dos cavaleiros o rosto de Leopoldo III, rei dos belgas na época do roubo.

fontes.trecho: Hubert Van Eyck between 1430 and 1432. [...] The panel was stolen in 1934 and has never been found. [...] The panel was displayed at the Saint Bavo Cathedral in Ghent, Belgium, together with the rest of the Ghent Altarpiece, until it was stolen during the night of 10 April 1934, possibly by the Belgian Arsène Goedertier [...] On 30 April, the Bishop of Ghent received a ransom demand for one million Belgian francs, to which the Belgian minister refused to agree. [...] Correspondence continued through October between the thief and the government, with the exchange of at least 11 letters. In an act of good faith, the ransomer returned one of the panel's two parts (a grisaille painting of St John the Baptist). On 25 November 1934 the self-proclaimed thief, Arsène Goedertier, revealed on his deathbed to his lawyer that he was the only one who knew where the masterpiece was hidden, and that he would take the secret to his grave. [...] De Vos found carbon copies of the ransom notes, and an unsent note that said "[it] rests in a place where neither I, nor anybody else, can take it away without arousing the attention of the public." [...] The police concluded that Goedertier had been the thief. [...] extensive searches have been held to locate it including an X-ray of the whole cathedral to a depth of 10 metres (33 ft). The panel has never been recovered and is now believed to have been destroyed. [...] The panel was replaced in 1945 by a copy made by Belgian restorer and copyist Jef Van der Veken. [...] He subtly indicated his work was a copy by giving one of the horsemen the facial features of Leopold III, who was the reigning King of the Belgians at the time the panel was stolen and the copy made.

gancho: Um museu dos EUA pagou 10 milhões de dólares por uma estátua grega e chegou a exibi-la com a etiqueta "Grécia, cerca de 530 a.C., ou falsificação moderna". A dúvida nunca foi resolvida.
explicacao: É o kouros do Museu Getty, em Los Angeles, uma estátua de jovem em mármore, maior que o tamanho natural, comprada em 1985. Os papéis que a acompanhavam diziam que ela estava numa coleção de Genebra desde 1930. Mas uma carta de 1952, atribuída ao maior especialista em escultura grega da época, tinha um código postal que só passou a existir em 1972, e uma conta bancária citada numa carta de 1955 só foi aberta em 1963. A papelada era uma farsa elaborada. A estátua em si, porém, continua dividindo os especialistas. O mármore veio provavelmente da ilha grega de Tasos, e detalhes como um sutil movimento do corpo para a direita, típico desse tipo de escultura, são tidos como forte indício de autenticidade. Já o estilo mistura traços que em outros kouroi aparecem com até um século de distância, algo muito incomum. E foi demonstrado um modo artificial de produzir a alteração química vista na superfície da pedra, que antes parecia sinal de idade. Se for autêntica, é um dos apenas doze kouroi completos conhecidos. Se for falsa, é obra de um falsário muito sofisticado e nunca identificado. Em 2018, o museu a tirou de exposição por causa da dúvida.

fontes.trecho: The Getty kouros is an over-life-sized statue in the form of a late archaic Greek kouros. The dolomitic marble sculpture was bought by the J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles, California, in 1985 for $10 million [...] Subsequent demonstration of an artificial means of creating the de-dolomitization observed on the stone has prompted a number of art historians to revise their opinions of the work. If genuine, it is one of only twelve extant complete kouroi. If fake, it exhibits a high degree of technical and artistic sophistication by an as-yet unidentified forger. Its status has remained undetermined: latterly the museum's label read "Greek, about 530 B.C., or modern forgery". Timothy Potts, the  director of the Getty, said that the sculpture was removed from display in 2018 due to its disputed authenticity. [...] These documents traced the provenance of the piece to a collection in Geneva of Dr. Jean Lauffenberger who, it was claimed, had bought it in 1930 from a Greek dealer. [...] Amongst the papers was a suspect 1952 letter allegedly from Ernst Langlotz, then the preeminent scholar of Greek sculpture [...] Later inquiries by the Getty revealed that the postcode on the Langlotz letter did not exist until 1972, and that a bank account mentioned in a 1955 letter to an A.E. Bigenwald regarding repairs on the statue was not opened until 1963. The documentary history of the sculpture was evidently an elaborate fake [...] Anachronizing elements are not unknown in authentic kouroi, but the disparity of up to a century is a strikingly unusual feature of the Getty sculpture. [...] Therefore, the statue is making motion toward his right, which Ilse Kleemann asserts is "one of the strongest pieces of evidence of its authenticity". [...] With the high dolomite content Thasos was determined to be the likeliest source with a 90% probability.

gancho: O Mapa de Vinlândia, revelado por Yale em 1965 como prova medieval de que os nórdicos chegaram à América, é falso. Uma das pistas: ele repete erros que só existem numa cópia impressa em 1782.
explicacao: O mapa surgiu em 1957, encadernado com um texto medieval, e mostra a sudoeste da Groenlândia uma terra chamada Vinlanda Insula, que teria sido visitada por europeus no século XI. Um ex-aluno de Yale, Paul Mellon, comprou-o por cerca de 300 mil dólares e o doou à universidade, que o apresentou ao mundo com um livro acadêmico na véspera do Dia de Colombo de 1965. Especialistas em documentos medievais desconfiaram assim que surgiram as fotos. Em análises iniciadas em 1972, a equipe do químico forense Walter McCrone achou nas linhas amareladas da tinta anatásio (dióxido de titânio) em cristais arredondados, exatamente a forma fabricada para pigmentos claros só a partir dos anos 1920. Mais tarde, o pesquisador John Paul Floyd mostrou que o desenho não se baseia no mapa de Bianco, de 1436, mas num fac-símile impresso em 1782, cujos erros, que não aparecem em nenhum outro lugar, o falso repete. Especialistas de Yale declararam que a pesquisa tinha estabelecido de forma conclusiva que se trata de uma falsificação moderna. A ironia é que os nórdicos chegaram mesmo à América: o sítio de L'Anse aux Meadows, na Terra Nova, foi descoberto em 1960, três anos depois de o mapa aparecer. O falso continua guardado na biblioteca de livros raros de Yale.

fontes.trecho: The Vinland Map is a 20th-century forgery purporting to be a 15th-century mappa mundi with unique information about Norse exploration of North America. The map first came to light in 1957 and was acquired by Yale University. [...] the map depicts a landmass south-west of Greenland in the Atlantic labelled as Vinland (Vinlanda Insula). The map describes this region as having been visited by Europeans in the 11th century. [...] historians of geography and medieval document specialists began to suspect that it might be a fake as soon as photographs of it became available. [...] specialists at Yale declared that the latest scientific and historical research had conclusively established that it was a modern forgery. The map remains in Yale University's Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library as part of its collection. [...] The Vinland map first came to light in 1957 (three years before the discovery of the Norse site at L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland in 1960), bound in a slim volume with a short medieval text [...] Yale contacted another alumnus, Paul Mellon, who agreed to buy it (for a price later stated to be about $300,000) and donate it to the university [...] The book was published, and the map revealed to the world, the day before Columbus Day, 1965. [...] In 1972, with new technology becoming available, Yale sent the map for chemical analysis by forensic specialist Walter McCrone whose team, using a variety of techniques, found that the yellowish lines contain anatase (titanium dioxide) in a rounded crystalline form manufactured for use in pale pigments since the 1920s, indicating that the ink was modern. [...] historical investigations by John Paul Floyd have revealed that the Vinland Map is based not on Bianco’s 1436 map, but on a printed facsimile map made in 1782. Floyd discovered this by noting mistakes in the 1782 map that were replicated on the Vinland map, but could be found nowhere else.

gancho: Segundo biógrafos da época, o jovem Michelangelo envelheceu de propósito um Cupido que esculpiu, para vendê-lo como antiguidade. O cardeal que o comprou descobriu a farsa, mas a obra lhe abriu as portas de Roma.
explicacao: Michelangelo tinha cerca de 20 anos quando começou a obra, em 1495, em Florença. O episódio chegou até nós pelos primeiros biógrafos, Ascanio Condivi, que escreveu com a colaboração do próprio Michelangelo, e Paolo Giovio. As versões variam sobre quem teve a ideia, e Vasari não o menciona nas Vidas. Michelangelo havia estudado uma escultura de cupido adormecido nos jardins dos Médici. Por conselho de Lorenzo di Pierfrancesco, envelheceu artificialmente o mármore para que parecesse antigo e fosse vendido por um preço maior. A peça passou a um negociante, Baldassare del Milanese, e acabou comprada pelo cardeal Riario de San Giorgio. Quando descobriu que o envelhecimento era falso, o cardeal exigiu o dinheiro de volta, mas Michelangelo pôde ficar com a sua parte. Ao saber quanto o negociante tinha lucrado, o escultor se ofereceu para pegar a estátua de volta. Baldassare recusou: preferia quebrá-la em cem pedaços, porque tinha comprado o menino e ele era propriedade sua. Mesmo com a fraude, foi essa obra que chamou para Michelangelo a atenção dos mecenas de Roma e ajudou a firmar sua reputação. Depois, a estátua passou por Cesare Borgia e Isabella d'Este e provavelmente foi parar na coleção de Carlos I da Inglaterra. O Cupido está perdido: o mais provável é que tenha sido destruído no grande incêndio do Palácio de Whitehall, em Londres, em 1698.

fontes.trecho: The Sleeping Cupid is a now-lost sculpture created by Renaissance artist Michelangelo, which he artificially aged to make it look like an antique on the advice of Lorenzo di Pierfrancesco in order to sell for a higher price. It was this sculpture which first brought him to the attention of patrons in Rome. [...] Michelangelo, about 20 years old, began working on his sleeping cupid in 1495, in Florence, Italy. Michelangelo never said why he carved a sculpture of a cupid, but it is known that he studied a sculpture in the Medici Gardens that contained a sleeping cupid. [...] Michelangelo created the sculpture and then passed it onto a dealer, Baldassare del Milanese. Eventually the sleeping cupid was bought by Cardinal Riario of San Giorgio; controversy arose when he discovered the statue was falsely aged and demanded his money back. However, Michelangelo was permitted to keep his share of the money. When Michelangelo offered to take the sculpture back from Baldassare when he learned how much money he made off of selling it, Baldassare refused, saying, "he would rather break it into a hundred pieces; he had bought the child, and it was his property". The Sleeping Cupid was a significant work in establishing the reputation of the young Michelangelo [...] The sculpture was later donated by Cesare Borgia to Isabella d'Este, and was probably collected by Charles I of England [...] In 1698, the Sleeping Cupid was most likely destroyed in the great fire in the Palace of Whitehall, London

Michelangelo, it seems, set out to create a sculpture that could be passed off as an ancient original. His early biographer, Paolo Giovio (1483-1552), wrote: [...] Michelangelo attained the highest fame in sculpture when he made an Eros out of marble and, after having kept it buried in the earth for a time and then bringing it to light again, so that owing to the stains and marks that it had acquired, as well as other minor imperfections which had intentionally been inflicted upon it, the Eros simulated a work of antiquity. Then he sold it for a great price through a middleman to Cardinal Riario. [...] He became Michelangelo’s first patron in Rome [...] Giorgio Vasari, does not mention the story of Michelangelo’s Sleeping Eros in his canonical Lives of the Artists [...] Another contemporary biographer, Ascanio Condivi (1525-74), does tells the story, but with the twist that Sleeping Eros had already been sculpted by Michelangelo in Florence, but an offer from a slippery art dealer promised to set Michelangelo up in Rome, if he could sell the statue as an ancient Roman original. Condivi’s biography is an “authorised” account, however: Michelangelo cooperated with Condivi in exchange for control over what was included

gancho: Uma "Natividade" de Caravaggio sumiu de Palermo em 1969. Delatores da Máfia já disseram que ela virou tapete de um chefão, que foi comida por ratos e porcos e que foi vendida para ser cortada em pedaços.
explicacao: O quadro, tradicionalmente datado de 1609, tem cerca de 2,7 metros de altura; por muito tempo se acreditou que foi pintado na Sicília, um ano antes da morte do artista. Na noite de 17 para 18 de outubro de 1969, dois ladrões o cortaram da moldura no Oratório de São Lourenço e levaram também um tapete, provavelmente para enrolá-lo. Em 2005, o FBI pôs o caso na sua lista dos dez maiores crimes contra a arte. Os investigadores em geral concordam que a Máfia siciliana cuidou do destino da obra depois do roubo, mas as versões se contradizem. Um informante disse ter visto o quadro usado como tapete pelo chefão Salvatore Riina. Outro, que disse ter participado do roubo, contou que o comprador chorou e desistiu ao ver o estrago. Em 2009, um terceiro relatou ter ouvido na prisão que a pintura foi escondida num celeiro, destruída por ratos e porcos e queimada, versão vista com dúvida por algumas autoridades. Em 2018, outro delator disse que ela foi vendida a um negociante suíço, avisado de que seria cortada em pedaços para o transporte. Já uma unidade dos Carabinieri acha que os ladrões eram amadores que souberam do valor da obra por um programa de TV. Desde 2015, uma réplica feita com alta tecnologia ocupa o altar.

fontes.titulo: Nativity with St. Francis and St. Lawrence
fontes.trecho: The Nativity with Saint Francis and Saint Lawrence is a painting of the nativity of Jesus from 1609 by Italian painter Caravaggio. It has been missing since 1969 when it was stolen from the Oratory of Saint Lawrence in Palermo. [...] A replica was commissioned in 2015 [...] It was believed to have been painted in Sicily, one year before Caravaggio died. [...] The painting is about 2.7 metres high and two metres wide. On the night of 17–18 October 1969, two thieves stole the painting from its home in the Oratory of Saint Lawrence in Palermo. They cut the painting from its frame, and also took a carpet from the oratory which authorities believe was used to roll up the painting. [...] The United States Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) listed it among their "Top Ten Art Crimes" in 2005. [...] investigators generally agree that the Sicilian Mafia has largely been responsible for the painting's subsequent movements. One Mafia informant recalled seeing it being used as a floor mat by the Sicilian Mafia boss Salvatore Riina. [...] In 2005, Mafia member Francesco Marino Mannoia told investigators that he was involved in the theft. He claimed that the painting was stolen on commission, and the private buyer wept and called off the sale when he saw how damaged it was from the robbery. [...] They believe the robbery was carried out by amateurs who learned about the painting's value on a television program about artifacts in Italy [...] In 2009, Mafia informant Gaspare Spatuzza told authorities that when he was in prison with Mafia member Filippo Graviano in 1999, Graviano told him the painting was destroyed in the 1980s. [...] Inside the barn, it was slowly destroyed by rats and pigs, and so was burnt. This story is doubted by some authorities. [...] In 2018, informant Gaetano Grado told authorities the painting was stolen by amateur criminals [...] The informant claims Badalamenti sold the painting to a Swiss dealer and told him it would be cut into pieces for transportation.

gancho: O quadro mais caro já leiloado, o "Salvator Mundi", vendido por 450,3 milhões de dólares como Leonardo, tinha sido comprado em 2005 por 1.175 dólares, como cópia. A autoria ainda é disputada.
explicacao: A pintura mostra Cristo abençoando com uma mão e segurando uma esfera de cristal com a outra. Existem cerca de trinta cópias e variações feitas por alunos e seguidores de Leonardo. Em 1958, ela foi leiloada por 45 libras como obra de um aluno dele, Boltraffio. Em 2005, num leilão em Nova Orleans, com o título "A partir de Leonardo da Vinci", dois marchands a compraram toda repintada e encomendaram a restauração. Fotos infravermelhas revelaram um arrependimento: o polegar da mão que abençoa tinha sido pintado antes mais erguido, o que torna bem menos provável que o quadro seja uma cópia. Mas a restauração foi tão extensa que a obra já foi chamada de "trabalho contemporâneo". Em 2017, a Christie's a vendeu por 450,3 milhões de dólares e disse que a maioria dos grandes estudiosos a considera um Leonardo; alguns especialistas, porém, acham que ele fez só partes dela, e outros negam a autoria. Há ainda um detalhe intrigante: uma esfera maciça de cristal deveria mostrar o que está atrás dela aumentado e invertido, mas no quadro o tecido atrás dela aparece quase sem distorção. Para o biógrafo Walter Isaacson, foi uma escolha consciente de Leonardo; para o historiador Charles Hope, que nega a autoria, é um indício contra ela. A obra não é exibida em público desde o leilão e, segundo relatos, está guardada na Arábia Saudita desde o fim de 2020.

fontes.trecho: Christie's, which sold the work in 2017, stated that most leading scholars consider it an original work by Leonardo, but this attribution has been disputed by some leading specialists who propose that he only contributed certain elements [...] The painting depicts Jesus Christ in anachronistic blue Renaissance attire, making a gesture of blessing with his right hand, while holding a transparent, non-refracting crystal orb in his left [...] Approximately thirty copies and variations of the work by pupils and followers of Leonardo have been identified [...] The painting was sold at auction for US$450.3 million on 15 November 2017 by Christie's in New York [...] setting a new record for the most expensive painting ever sold at public auction. [...] The painting has not been publicly exhibited since the 2017 Christie's auction, and since late 2020 has been in storage in Saudi Arabia reportedly awaiting a museum [...] sold it at auction in 1958 for £45 (equivalent to £900 in 2025) as a work by Leonardo's pupil Giovanni Antonio Boltraffio [...] In 2005, the estate of Baton Rouge businessman Basil Clovis Hendry Sr. was auctioned by St. Charles Gallery in New Orleans. Lot 664 was titled "After Leonardo da Vinci: Christ Salvator Mundi". Art dealers Alexander Parish and Robert Simon, an Old Master specialist, bought it for $1,175 [...] It was heavily overpainted [...] In April 2005, they commissioned Dianne Dwyer Modestini at New York University to oversee the restoration. Infrared photographs revealed a pentimento where the blessing hand's thumb is more upright. The artist's alteration of the thumb made it far less likely that the painting was a copy. [...] Her restoration was so extensive that Salvator Mundi has been called a "contemporary work" [...] Leonardo failed to paint the distortion that would occur when looking through a solid clear orb at objects that are not touching the orb. Solid glass or crystal, whether shaped like an orb or a lens, produces magnified, inverted, and reversed images. Instead, Leonardo painted the orb as if it were a hollow glass bubble that does not refract or distort the light passing through it. Isaacson believes that this was "a conscious decision on Leonardo's part" [...] The British art historian Charles Hope dismissed the attribution to Leonardo entirely in a January 2020 analysis of the painting's quality and provenance. He doubted that Leonardo would have painted a work where the eyes were not level and the drapery undistorted by a crystal orb.

gancho: Em 2019, ladrões puseram fogo numa caixa de energia para apagar a luz da rua e levaram joias do Grünes Gewölbe, em Dresden. Na saída, recolocaram as grades da janela para atrasar a descoberta.
explicacao: O Grünes Gewölbe, ou Abóbada Verde, fundado em 1723 por Augusto, o Forte, eleitor da Saxônia e rei da Polônia, é um dos museus mais antigos da Europa. Às 4 da manhã de 25 de novembro de 2019, um pequeno incêndio numa ponte vizinha destruiu uma caixa de energia. O apagão desligou a iluminação da rua e os alarmes, mas as câmeras continuaram gravando. Os ladrões cortaram as barras de ferro de uma janela, num buraco tão estreito que, segundo a polícia, só gente bem magra passaria, e quebraram as vitrines a machado. Levaram peças de conjuntos de joias do século XVIII e o Diamante Branco de Dresden, de 62 quilates. Algumas joias ficaram porque estavam costuradas ao fundo do armário. A joia mais famosa do museu, o Diamante Verde de Dresden, escapou por estar emprestada ao Metropolitan, em Nova York. Seis jovens do clã Remmo, de Berlim, foram acusados. Dois deles já cumpriam pena pelo roubo de uma moeda de ouro de 100 quilos do Museu Bode, em 2017, que nunca foi recuperada. Em 2022, trinta e uma peças voltaram depois que os advogados dos acusados revelaram onde estavam, e em 2023 cinco membros da família foram condenados.

fontes.trecho: On 25 November 2019, royal jewellery was stolen from the Green Vault museum within Dresden Castle in Dresden, Saxony, Germany. The stolen items included the 62-carat Dresden White Diamond [...] In 2022, thirty-one of the stolen items were recovered by the German authorities in Berlin, reportedly after talks with the lawyers of six men on trial for the theft. [...] one of the oldest museums in Europe, founded in 1723 by Augustus II the Strong, Elector of Saxony and King of Poland. [...] One of the museum's main treasures, the 41-carat Dresden Green Diamond, was away on loan at New York's Metropolitan Museum of Art. [...] On 25 November 2019, at 4 a.m. a small fire was started on the nearby Augustus Bridge, which destroyed a power box. The resulting power outage disabled streetlights and security alarms, but CCTV continued to function. The thieves then cut through iron bars around a window to break into the museum's Jewel Room. According to police, the thieves must have been very small to fit through the hole. [...] They smashed the glass displays with an axe to gain access to the jewellery. The thieves removed three 18th-century jewellery sets [...] some jewellery was sewn into the surface of the cabinet and those pieces remained. [...] The thieves exited through the same window, replacing the bars in order to delay detection. [...] In September 2021, German prosecutors charged six men over the theft [...] who belong to the Remmo Clan, an infamous family of Mhallami background in Berlin [...] Two of the suspects were already serving sentences for participating in another major heist, the theft of a 100-kilogram Canadian gold coin dubbed the "Big Maple Leaf" from Berlin's Bode Museum in 2017. The coin, with an estimated value of  €3.75 million, has not been recovered. [...] On May 16, 2023, five members of the Remmo family were convicted by a court in Dresden.

gancho: Na sexta-feira de carnaval de 2006, ladrões levaram quadros de Picasso, Dalí, Matisse e Monet de um museu do Rio e sumiram entre os foliões de um bloco. As obras nunca apareceram, e o crime prescreveu em 2026.
explicacao: O Museu da Chácara do Céu, em Santa Teresa, foi a casa do colecionador Raymundo Ottoni de Castro Maya. Na tarde de 24 de fevereiro de 2006, enquanto o bloco das Carmelitas desfilava pelas ladeiras do bairro, homens armados entraram como visitantes, pagaram o ingresso e anunciaram o assalto. Renderam os seguranças, que não andavam armados, juntaram funcionários e turistas na sala de segurança, desligaram as câmeras e levaram as fitas. Foram direto ao que queriam: "A Dança", de Picasso; "Os Dois Balcões", de Dalí, o único quadro do pintor exposto ao público na América Latina, segundo a diretora; "O Jardim de Luxemburgo", de Matisse; "Marinha", de Monet; e um livro de gravuras de Picasso. Fugiram e se misturaram à multidão da festa. Dias depois, a Polícia Federal achou restos queimados de quadros e molduras num morro vizinho, e uma moldura foi identificada, de início, como a do Picasso. Um detalhe ficou sem a devida atenção dos investigadores: o Dalí e o Matisse já tinham sido roubados do mesmo museu em 1989 e achados logo depois. Houve suspeitos, mas nenhuma investigação deu em nada. Em fevereiro de 2026, 20 anos depois, o crime prescreveu, e ninguém mais poderá ser punido por ele.

fontes.titulo: 'No one was really interested in finding those works': major Brazilian art theft still unsolved as statute of limitations expires
fontes.trecho: Two decades after one of the biggest art thefts in Brazilian history, the statute of limitations has expired. This means no one will ever face prison time for stealing five works by Claude Monet, Henri Matisse, Salvador Dalí and Pablo Picasso in 2006 from the Museu da Chácara do Céu in Rio de Janeiro. The four paintings and book of prints have yet to be recovered, and those responsible were never identified. [...] On the afternoon of 24 February 2006, during Rio’s Carnival [...] disabled the security cameras and took the surveillance tapes. Minutes later, they fled on foot with the works of art, disappearing into the crowds outside. [...] Chácara do Céu is the former home of the businessman and art collector Raymundo Ottoni de Castro Maya [...] Over the past 20 years, a few suspects emerged in the heist but none of the investigations led anywhere. [...] investigators failed to revisit an important fact later highlighted by a journalistic investigation: the museum had already been robbed in 1989, and some of the works stolen in 2006 had also been taken in that earlier theft and recovered.

fontes.titulo: Thieves disappear into Carnival crowds after robbing museum (Chicago Tribune)
fontes.trecho: The robbers approached the museum as visitors. While two of them waited in a van by the front gate, the other four paid their entrance fee and started toward the galleries. Then upon announcing the robbery, they brandished guns and at least one grenade. They overpowered the security guards, who worked for a private firm and were unarmed. They herded visitors and museum staff into the security office, where they disconnected the closed-circuit security cameras and ripped out any videotapes that might have captured them on film. And they collected their loot: Pablo Picasso’s “The Dance”; Dali’s “The Two Balconies”; Henri Matisse’s “Luxembourg Garden”; Claude Monet’s “Marine”; and a book of Picasso engravings illustrating poems by Pablo Neruda. [...] The Dali, for example, is the only painting by the Spanish surrealist on public exhibition in Latin America, said museum director Vera de Alencar. [...] they went past everything else and went straight for what they wanted. [...] Indeed, the Dali and the Matisse were stolen once before from the same museum. That happened in 1989, and the works were quickly found.

fontes.titulo: Painting stolen from Rio de Janeiro museum may have been burned (Agência Brasil)
fontes.trecho: The Federal Police found this Thursday (2) burned residues of paintings and frames, in Morro dos Prazeres, an area nearby the Chácara do Céu Museum [...] a preliminary procedure identified one of the frames as that of Picasso’s painting "The Dance".

fontes.titulo: Após 20 anos, roubo de obras de Monet, Picasso e Dalí prescreve no Rio (Agência Brasil)
fontes.trecho: Publicado em 22 de Fevereiro, 2026 [...] Era dia de apresentação do Bloco das Carmelitas, mas a cena não fazia parte da festa. [...] Passados 20 anos, o crime prescreve oficialmente nesta semana e os responsáveis pelo roubo não poderão mais ser punidos.

gancho: O Metropolitan de Nova York exibiu por décadas três guerreiros etruscos de terracota que eram falsos. Em 1961, um dos falsários confessou e, como prova, mostrou o polegar que faltava numa estátua: guardara de lembrança.
explicacao: As estátuas foram feitas pelos irmãos Pio e Alfonso Riccardi e três de seus filhos, com a ajuda do escultor Alfredo Fioravanti, e o museu as comprou entre 1915 e 1921. Ao "Velho Guerreiro", de 202 centímetros, faltavam o polegar esquerdo e o braço direito. Uma "Cabeça Colossal" fez os especialistas concluírem que ela vinha de uma estátua de sete metros. As três peças foram exibidas juntas pela primeira vez em 1933. Historiadores, sobretudo italianos, desconfiaram pelo estilo, mas faltava prova. Em 1960, testes acharam manganês no esmalte, ingrediente que os etruscos nunca usaram. O museu só se convenceu quando os peritos entenderam como as peças tinham sido feitas. Os falsários não tinham habilidade nem um forno grande o bastante para estátuas daquele tamanho. Então as esculpiam, pintavam com esmalte e as derrubavam ainda cruas, para queimar os pedaços. Os fragmentos eram "descobertos" e vendidos ou remontados, como numa restauração. Em 5 de janeiro de 1961, Fioravanti entrou no consulado americano em Roma, assinou uma confissão e apresentou o polegar. Em 15 de fevereiro, o Metropolitan anunciou que as estátuas eram falsificações.

fontes.trecho: The Etruscan terracotta warriors are three statues that resemble the work of the ancient Etruscans, but are in fact art forgeries. The statues, created by Italian brothers Pio and Alfonso Riccardi and three of their six sons, were bought by The Metropolitan Museum of Art between 1915 and 1921. [...] In 1908, Fuschini informed the British Museum that the chariot had been found in the old Etruscan fort near Orvieto [...] The British Museum bought the chariot and published the find in 1912. [...] The Riccardis enlisted the aid of sculptor Alfredo Fioravanti and created a statue, later known as the Old Warrior. It was 202 cm (6.6 ft) tall and was naked from the waist down. It was also missing its left thumb and right arm. In 1915, they sold it to the Metropolitan Museum of Art that also bought their next work, the Colossal Head, in 1916. Experts decided it must have been part of a seven-metre (23-foot) statue. [...] The three warrior statues were first exhibited together in 1933. In the following years, various art historians, especially in Italy, presented their suspicions that on stylistic and artistic grounds alone, the statues might be forgeries, but there was no forensic proof to support the allegations. [...] In 1960, chemical tests of the statue glazes showed the presence of manganese, an ingredient that Etruscans had never used. The museum was not convinced until experts deduced how they had been made. The statues had been sculpted, painted with glaze, then toppled while in an unfired, green state to produce fragments. [...] This was confirmed by Alfredo Fioravanti, who on January 5, 1961, entered the US consulate in Rome and signed a confession. The forgers had lacked the skills – and the very large kiln – required to make such large pieces. The fragments had been fired, "discovered" and sold, or re-assembled ("restored") then sold. As proof, Fioravanti presented the Old Warrior's missing thumb, which he had kept as a memento. On February 15, the Metropolitan Museum announced that the statues were forgeries.
